summary: Verona Beach Light, a conical concrete tower lit in 1917 at the east end of Oneida Lake; owned by New York State Canals, cared for by a local association; grounds open, tower closed.

structures.type: conical concrete tower of prefabricated sections
structures.note: 84.5 ft from base to lantern centre (Society record); 'a half-foot shorter' than the two sister towers (Lighthouse Friends)

events.note: Tower established 1917 (Society record). Work began 1916 under state contract 132 (Lighthouse Friends). Tug 44 and Lighthouse Digest date the design or build to 1915; the association's website says the lights have been there since 1915.
Lit for the first time in the late summer of 1917, with a gas beacon behind an exposed glass lens (Lighthouse Friends)
Gas cylinder fuel system replaced by commercial electric service to power the beacon (Lighthouse Digest)
Verona Beach Lighthouse Association took shape to restore and maintain the tower (association site)
Tower given a new coat of white paint (Tug 44)

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Lighthouse Friends dates the contract and start of work to 1916 and the first light to late summer 1917. The Society's record gives 1917 as the tower year. Tug 44 gives 1917 for the build and says the design was 1915. Lighthouse Digest says all three towers were built in 1915, and the association's website says the lights have been there since 1915. This record uses 1916 for the start of work and 1917 for the first light, and reports the 1915 dates as disagreements.
Lighthouse Friends and the Erie Canal Foundation date completion of the Barge Canal to 1918; Tug 44 ties the tower's build to a 1917 opening. This record follows the 1918 date for the canal.

notes_for_editor: 1) Status conflict: the station record says inactive, taken from the Society's 'Active Aid to Navigation?: No'. Lighthouse Friends, Lighthouse Digest, Tug 44 and the association site all describe it as active. The story gives both. 2) Characteristic: the record's Fl W 4s comes from ENC; Lighthouse Friends describes the original light as occulting white. No characteristic is put in facts. 3) HAER documentation exists (a Library of Congress item titled New York State Barge Canal, Sylvan Beach Lighthouse, End of Fourth Avenue, Verona Beach, Oneida County, NY), found in a web search. fetch_text returned HTTP 403 for loc.gov/item/ny2230, so it is not read and not cited. It is the first thing to read for design and construction. 4) Newspapers: a Chronicling America search of New York papers for 'Verona Beach' with 'light' (1915 to 1921) found no hits; 'Verona Beach' with 'lighthouse' (1900 to 1925) found none; 'Oneida Lake' with 'light' (1916 to 1918) found seven hits in The Sun, none read as being about the tower. 5) Keepers: no keeper of this tower is named in any source read; the Society roster is empty. The keeper paragraph describes the state's system from Lighthouse Friends, labelled there as general context, not tower-specific. 6) Lighthouse Friends, Lighthouse Digest, Tug 44 and the association site are treated as copyrighted: paraphrased, with one short quotation each. 7) The association's officers are not named; the Digest's treasurer is named only as 'the association's treasurer'. 8) NRHP and the state's own canal records were not checked. 9) The USLHS record says 'Open to Public: No'; Lighthouse Friends says grounds open, tower closed. The story follows Lighthouse Friends: grounds open, tower closed. 10) No storms, collisions or rescues found. Fact-check 2026-10-28: the opening height now says the 84.5 ft figure is to the lantern centre, not the tower's full height; the Sylvan Beach amusement-park detail was removed (it is not about this light); Lighthouse Digest's about-80-foot figure, Lighthouse Friends' electric-power statement and the association's 1915 date were added as disagreements; most quotations from the copyrighted sources were rewritten in the story's own words.
